title: Smallest.ai raises $13M to build ultra-fast voice AI that sounds genuinely human
slides: Smallest.ai raised $13M. Why does voice AI still sound robotic?
Their model responds in under 200 milliseconds.

thread_text:
1. The $13M bet

Voice AI raised millions, yet your customers can still tell they're talking to a machine. That gap is the opening.

2. Under 200ms

Smallest.ai's model cuts response time below the human threshold. The robotic lag disappears entirely.

3. Human pauses

It doesn't just spit words—it mimics natural silence. That changes how customers perceive the conversation.

4. Scripts are dead

Forget your call center flow. This AI adapts to the caller, not your pre-written prompts. Your training is obsolete.

5. Test it now

Put your best agent against their demo this week. If the AI wins, what's your next move?

instagram.caption:
You answer a customer in under 200 milliseconds, or they hear robotic lag. That's the new bar.

Smallest.ai just raised $13M for a voice model that hits that threshold and mimics human pauses—silence included, not just words. It adapts to the caller on the fly.

That means your pre-written call center scripts don't map anymore. The AI doesn't follow your flow; it reads the person. Your training materials are already behind.

For anyone building voice agents or phone systems: the benchmark isn't "sounds okay." It's beating your best human rep in a blind test. So run that test this week. Put your top agent against their demo—what does your customer experience actually lose? 🗣️⚡
